title: Jobs
goal: Name jobs and the things people use to do them, and follow a simple instruction at work.

grammar.example: She is a vet. He is an artist.

vocabulary.example: The vet helps sick animals.
A dog came in. He is hurt.
Bring the cat inside.
The dog is sick today.
Here is the bandage. Thank you!
Give the medicine to the dog.
The firefighter is very brave.
Put water on the fire.
The water puts the fire out.
Climb the ladder to the window.
Put on the helmet first.
The truck is red and very loud.
The chef makes a birthday cake.
Crack the egg into the bowl.
Add the milk and mix it.
Put it in the pan.
Serve the cake, please.
Careful, the pan is hot!
Can you help me, please?
My mother goes to work at eight.

phrases.text: What do you want to be?
I want to be a vet.
phrases.use: Answering. Say a vet, not just vet.
An instruction at work. No please needed in an emergency.
A warning. Say it fast and loud.
Praising someone who did the work well.

lines.text: Good morning! A dog came in. He is hurt.
Poor dog. Get the bandage, please.
Thank you. Now give the medicine.
Good job. A cat is waiting at the door. Bring the cat inside.
The cat is safe. You are a great vet!

questions.q: What does the dog need first?
Who is waiting at the door?

speaking.text: I want to be a vet.
speaking.tip: Want to often sounds like wanna in fast speech.
Put on links into one word: pu-ton.
The b in climb is silent. Say clime.
Help me is one push of air. Don't stop between them.

writing.question: What do you want to be?

quiz.q: A firefighter puts ___ on the fire.
What do you put on your head before a fire?

options: I want to be a vet.
